**Tesla – recent whirlwind of product, financial and strategic moves (late Oct 2026)**  

- **Product setbacks** – Tesla cancelled the Cybertruck rollout in Australia and New Zealand, notifying customers by email on Oct 23 [1].  
- **Flying Roadster hype** – The company unveiled a “flying” version of the Roadster, claiming it can hit 60 mph in under a second; production is now slated for 2028, but traders remain skeptical after years of delays [2][15][16][17].  
- **Financial pressure** – Q3 2026 earnings showed a 43 % profit drop and a 3 % dip in automotive revenue, while energy‑generation/storage fell 16 % [3][4]; analysts warn Tesla may be nearing unprofitability [20].  
- **Regulatory & safety concerns** – A Full‑Self‑Driving (now “Tesla Assisted Driving”) vehicle struck and killed a pedestrian on I‑80, raising safety questions [8][19].  
- **Merger speculation** – SpaceX and Tesla are being discussed as a potential merger; any deal would need Elon Musk’s sign‑off and faces political, regulatory and investor scrutiny [7][9][10][11][12].  
- **Political spending** – Musk has poured $366 million into election campaigns, betting on a Senate outcome that could affect SpaceX/Tesla regulation [5].  
- **Long‑term vision** – Musk reiterated that autonomous Teslas will dominate future travel, framing the company’s mission as “world domination” of transportation [6].  

*Overall picture*: Tesla is juggling major product delays and safety incidents while its finances weaken, all amid high‑stakes political spending and swirling rumors of a merger with SpaceX.
